classes.title: Class 1: Questions: Different types
classes.desc: Core rules, usage patterns, and practical sentence structures for different types of questions.

Distinguishing common traps, errors, and subtle register differences
Spoken fluency templates and IELTS/academic writing applications

questions.q: Which sentence illustrates correct usage of 'Questions: Different types'?
options: The committee agreed on the proposed framework regarding questions: different types.
The committee agreeing on the proposed framework regarding questions: different types.
The committee agree on proposed frameworks without agreement.
The committee is agree with the guidelines.
questions.answer: The committee agreed on the proposed framework regarding questions: different types.
questions.explanation: Expresses full subject-verb agreement and natural collocations for Questions: Different types.

questions.q: Identify the common error when applying 'Questions: Different types' in everyday communication:
options: Omitting auxiliary verbs or misplacing modifying clauses.
Using appropriate punctuation at the end of clauses.
Selecting precise synonyms in formal contexts.
Maintaining consistent tense throughout the discourse.
questions.answer: Omitting auxiliary verbs or misplacing modifying clauses.
questions.explanation: Learners frequently omit essential auxiliary verbs or fail to order clauses properly.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically sound option for this sentence (Questions: Different types):
options: Despite the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
Despite of the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
Although the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
In spite the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
questions.answer: Despite the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun phrase directly without 'of' (unlike 'in spite of').

questions.q: Which sentence correctly maintains subject-verb agreement under 'Questions: Different types' rules?
options: Neither the manager nor the assistants were available for comment.
Neither the manager nor the assistants was available for comment.
Neither the manager or the assistants were available for comment.
Neither the manager nor the assistants being available for comment.
questions.answer: Neither the manager nor the assistants were available for comment.
questions.explanation: With 'neither... nor...', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('assistants' -> 'were').

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition/connector for 'Questions: Different types':
"He succeeded in passing the exam ___ studying consistently every evening."
options: by
with
throughout
at
questions.answer: by
questions.explanation: Use 'by + gerund' to explain the method or manner through which something is achieved.

questions.q: Select the sentence with accurate punctuation and clause structure:
options: Although she was exhausted, she finished the entire assignment.
Although she was exhausted she finished, the entire assignment.
She finished the entire assignment, although, she was exhausted.
Although was exhausted, she finished the entire assignment.
questions.answer: Although she was exhausted, she finished the entire assignment.
questions.explanation: A subordinate clause at the start of a sentence is set off by a comma.

questions.q: Which expression provides the most natural academic register?
options: The findings indicate a substantial improvement in student retention.
The findings show a really big improvement in student retention.
The findings are saying that students stay more.
The findings tell that students get much better.
questions.answer: The findings indicate a substantial improvement in student retention.
questions.explanation: 'Indicate a substantial improvement' provides precise academic vocabulary appropriate for advanced writing.

questions.q: Identify the sentence that contains a grammatical error regarding 'Questions: Different types':
options: She suggested me to consult an academic advisor immediately.
She suggested that I consult an academic advisor immediately.
She recommended consulting an academic advisor immediately.
She advised me to consult an academic advisor immediately.
questions.answer: She suggested me to consult an academic advisor immediately.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' does not take object + infinitive (*suggest me to do*). Use 'suggest that...' or 'suggest + gerund'.

questions.q:
Choose the best alternative to replace the highlighted phrase for concise clarity:
"Owing to the fact that it was raining heavily..."
options: Because it was raining heavily
For reason that it rained
Due to because of the rain
Since that it was heavy rain
questions.answer: Because it was raining heavily
questions.explanation: 'Because' is more direct, natural, and avoids wordy redundant phrasing.

questions.q: Which sentence demonstrates the correct position of adverbs of frequency?

She always has been interested in linguistic anthropology.
Always she has been interested in linguistic anthropology.
She has been always interested in linguistic anthropology.
questions.answer: She has always been interested in linguistic anthropology.

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct subjunctive / formal structure:
"It is imperative that every member ___ the code of conduct."
options: follow
follows
followed
is following
questions.answer: follow
questions.explanation: The present subjunctive with 'imperative that' uses the base form 'follow' regardless of the subject.

questions.q:
Choose the correct collocated preposition:
"The company is committed ___ reducing its carbon emissions by 2030."
options: to
for
with
at
questions.answer: to
questions.explanation: 'Committed to' is followed by a gerund or noun phrase ('reducing').

questions.q:
Which option transforms the active sentence into a natural passive form?
Active: "Authorities have closed the bridge for inspection."

The bridge had been closed for inspection by authorities.
The bridge was being closed for inspection by authorities.
The bridge is closed for inspection since authorities.
questions.answer: The bridge has been closed for inspection by authorities.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive uses 'has/have been + past participle' ('has been closed').
